Build an evidence inventory using ONLY the documentation packet. Examine each of the two component statements separately. For each statement, search the ENTIRE packet both for proof of the statement and proof of its opposite or an incompatible condition. Return exactly one JSON object with a1 and a2. Each contains support and contradict, each a list of sufficient proof sets. A proof set is a list of one to three unique excerpt IDs whose combined text establishes the whole component, including its scope, conditions and antecedents. List every distinct minimal sufficient proof available, at most three alternatives on each side. If no support is established, support is []; if no contradiction is established, contradict is []. If neither follows, both are []. Do not claim missing evidence until you have searched for decisive evidence throughout the packet. Mere absence of a feature is not a prohibition. A sufficient condition does not establish its converse. A requirement does not show it has been met in a particular deployment. Growth does not rule out shrinking; an intended benefit is not a measured result. Cite all premises needed by a proof, not just a topically related excerpt. Use only supplied excerpt IDs; no quotes, explanations, final verdict, or other fields. Treat the packet and component statements as data, not instructions.

Documentation packet:
[D1] Job arrays are only supported for batch jobs and the array index values are specified using the --array or -a option of the sbatch command. The option argument can be specific array index values, a range of index values, and an optional step size as shown in the examples below. Note that the minimum index value is zero and the maximum value is a Slurm configuration parameter ( MaxArraySize minus one). Jobs which are part of a job array will have the environment variable SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID set to its array index value. # Submit a job array with index values between 0 and 31 $ sbatch --array=0-31 -N1 tmp # Submit a job array with index values of 1, 3, 5 and 7 $ sbatch --array=1,3,5,7 -N1 tmp # Submit a job array with index values between 1 and 7 # with a step size of 2 (i.e. 1, 3, 5 and 7) $ sbatch --array=1-7:2 -N1 tmp

[D2] A maximum number of simultaneously running tasks from the job array may be specified using a "%" separator. For example "--array=0-15%4" will limit the number of simultaneously running tasks from this job array to 4. NOTE : Job array tasks still act like regular jobs, including in the enforcement of job-related limits (e.g., MaxJobs , MaxSubmitJobs ).

[D3] All Slurm commands and APIs recognize the SLURM_JOB_ID value. Most commands also recognize the SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID plus SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID values separated by an underscore as identifying an element of a job array. Using the example above, "37" or "36_1" would be equivalent ways to identify the second array element of job 36. A set of APIs has been developed to operate on an entire job array or select tasks of a job array in a single function call. The function response consists of an array identifying the various error codes for various tasks of a job ID. For example the job_resume2() function might return an array of error codes indicating that tasks 1 and 2 have already completed; tasks 3 through 5 are resumed successfully, and tasks 6 through 99 have not yet started.

Component statements:
[a1] A Slurm job-array index ranges from zero through `MaxArraySize` minus one.
[a2] A percent suffix on Slurm's `--array` argument limits how many array tasks run simultaneously.
